To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the binding of ConA at the free apices of the surface cells in human breast tumor explants grown in vitro was studied cytochemicaly with HRP as a marker.
Con A binds to human breast cancer cell membranes in a temperature- and incubation time-dependent manner, with a discontinuous label that is topically stabilized at sites of membrane contact.

Con A binds to the cell membranes of human breast cancer explanted to organ culture, and that the Con A receptors are distributed over the entire cell surface, with the exception of the areas where two membranes or different parts of a folded membrane are in close contact.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution and redistribution of Con A receptors on the surface of human breast tumor cells.
the distribution of Con A receptors on the surface of breast cancer cells and their possible role in the development and progression of breast cancer.
the binding of lectins to the cell membranes of human breast cancer explant organ cultures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the distribution of Con A receptors on the cell surface is not uniform, that there are areas of high and low density of receptors, that the distribution is dynamic, that there are differences in the density of receptors in different areas of the cell surface and that there is an inverse correlation between the density of the Con A receptors and the degree of involution in the explant.

Con A receptors are distributed in a dispersed fashion on the surface of human mammary tumor cells in culture, and that the binding of ConA at 20 degrees or 37 degrees C results in the redistribution of these sites on the cell surface and their internalization.
the Con A binding sites were distributed on the surface of the cell in a random fashion and that their redistribution and internalization were dependent on temperature and incubation time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the binding, redistribution and internalization of Con A on the surface of breast cancer cells grown in organ culture is a function of the temperature of the binding reaction and of the incubation temperature.
the Con A binding sites are present at the apical membranes of the tumor cells in the organ cultures and are distributed in a discontinuous fashion.

the Con A receptors are present in a dispersed distribution on the free surfaces of human breast tumors in culture, and that their redistribution and internalization are induced by temperature-dependent processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distribution of Con A receptors on the surface of human breast cancer explant cells is dynamic.
the binding of ConA at the free apices of surface cancer cells in human breast explants grown in vitro can be studied cytochemcially with horseradishe peroxidase as a marker.

the Con A receptors are present on the surface of human breast cancer explant cells in organ culture and that the Con A binding and redistribution on the surface of these cells is temperature-dependent and is not related to the type of cancer studied.
